description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-ui/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md) and the store specs gamification ('Light and dark theme') and content-authoring (CA-D21). Pay attention to: the lint rule's false negatives (literal text it misses), whether the pseudo-catalog test can pass while a string bypasses the catalog, the theme and a11y e2e actually iterating every route, the provenance check's coverage of fixture/asset roots, nginx proxying and SPA fallback, the Dockerfile build with the contract submodule, and tsconfig splits leaking Node types into app code.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literal text inside object/array props and TS-wrapped literals
findings.evidence: `literalTexts` only handles Literal, TemplateLiteral, Conditional, Logical, `+` Binary and ExpressionContainer, and `default: return []`. So `<ChoiceGroup options={[{ value: 'a', label: 'Ano' }]} />` (ArrayExpression/ObjectExpression), `aria-label={'Zavřít' as const}` / `satisfies` / `!` (TSAsExpression etc.), `{['Ahoj']}` and `{'Ahoj'.toUpperCase()}` all lint clean. Literal option labels passed to design-system components are the obvious next pattern in the task/mission slices.
findings.suggestion: Recurse through TSAsExpression/TSSatisfiesExpression/TSNonNullExpression/ParenthesizedExpression/SequenceExpression (last expression), ArrayExpression elements and ObjectExpression property values, at least for text-like keys (label, title, text, …). Add the matching invalid cases to src/test/lint-rule.test.ts.

findings.title: Template literal check ignores literals nested in `${…}` expressions
findings.evidence: `case "TemplateLiteral": return node.quasis.map(...)` looks only at the static quasis. So `` {`${ok ? 'Ano' : 'Ne'}`} `` or `` aria-label={`${n} ${'bodů'}`} `` pass, because the letters sit in `node.expressions`.
findings.suggestion: Also return `node.expressions.flatMap(literalTexts)` and add an invalid test case for it.

findings.title: Visible-value detection needs a static `type` and skips other visible-text attributes
findings.evidence: `staticAttribute(opening, "type")` returns null unless the attribute value is a plain Literal. So `<input type={'submit'} value="Odeslat" />` passes. `defaultValue` and `value` on text inputs and textarea (prefilled visible text) are never checked, and neither is `label` on `<option>`/`<optgroup>`/`<track>`. The pseudo-catalog test's TEXT_ATTRIBUTES list misses `label` as well.
findings.suggestion: Unwrap a JSXExpressionContainer holding a Literal in `staticAttribute`. Add `label` to DOM_TEXT_ATTRIBUTES and to TEXT_ATTRIBUTES in i18n-coverage.test.tsx. Treat `defaultValue` as text on input and textarea.

findings.title: NFR-9 lint covers only JSX positions in .tsx files
findings.evidence: The rule is wired with `files: ['src/**/*.tsx']` and only inspects JSXText, JSXExpressionContainer and JSXAttribute. UI strings in `.ts` hooks or helpers (e.g. a `useMissionLabel()` returning 'Mise'), `document.title = 'X'`, or `const msg = 'Chyba'; … {msg}` are never reported. Only the pseudo-catalog render can catch these, and only if that state gets rendered (see the related finding).
findings.suggestion: Record this limit in the rule header and design.md. Optionally add a `document.title`/`*.textContent` assignment check and extend `files` to `src/**/*.ts` (excluding generated and test files) for that check.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test rejects punctuation-only or numeric text nodes that the lint rule explicitly allows
findings.evidence:
`COVERED` requires at least one `⟦…⟧` segment per text node, and each DOM text node is checked separately. The lint rule's valid case `

{t("a")} · {t("b")}

` renders separate text nodes `⟦a⟧`, ` · `, `⟦b⟧`, and the trimmed `·` fails COVERED. A bare numeric child like `{xp}` fails the same way. The two NFR-9 checks contradict each other, so the first slice that renders a separator or a number will fail the test or have to put digits in the catalog.
findings.suggestion: Accept text nodes made only of whitespace, digits, punctuation or symbols (e.g. `/^[\s\d\p{P}\p{S}]*$/u`), or check the concatenated textContent per element instead of each node. Add a test with a separator node and a numeric node.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test sees only the initial render, so conditional, loading and error strings can bypass it
findings.evidence: Each route is rendered once with `render(<App messages={pseudo} />)` and inspected synchronously. Error, empty, success and dialog states, and anything shown after a TanStack Query resolves or fails, are never in the DOM when `uiTexts` runs. A literal held in a variable or a .ts helper and shown only in those states passes both this test and the lint rule. CSS `content:` text is also not inspected.
findings.suggestion: Require each slice to register its screen states (e.g. a per-route `states` fixture with mocked query results) in the registry the test iterates. Also wait for queries to settle (`findBy…`/`waitFor`) before collecting texts.

findings.title: a11y and theme e2e never visit the not-found screen
findings.evidence: Both specs iterate `ROUTE_PATHS` (`['/']`), and `routes.test.ts` keeps that equal to `routes`. `App.tsx:19` renders `<NotFound />` for every other path, and nginx serves it for any unknown URL, so it is a real served screen. Yet no axe run, reduced-motion check or light/dark `--paper` check covers it. The i18n test does cover it, which shows it is meant to be in scope.
findings.suggestion: Add an unregistered path (e.g. '/no-such-route', asserting the NotFound heading instead of `[data-route]`) to the a11y and theme loops, or export a `SCREEN_PATHS` list that includes it.

findings.title: Theme 'no toggle' check swallows click failures and only inspects <html>
findings.evidence: `await control.click(...).catch(() => undefined)` silently skips any control that cannot be clicked, so the scenario 'every … toggle is activated' can pass without activating anything. With zero controls on '/' it passes vacuously. The DS selector `[data-theme="dark"]` (tokens.css:50) applies on any element, but the check only asserts `html` has no `data-theme` and reads body background. A toggle that sets `data-theme` on `<main>` would switch the visible theme and still pass.
findings.suggestion: Fail, or at least record, controls that could not be clicked, and log the activated-control count. Assert `page.locator('[data-theme]')` has count 0 and check the route root's computed background as well as body.

findings.title: nginx resolves `backend` once at startup; a backend restart or recreate leaves the proxy on a stale IP
findings.evidence: `proxy_pass http://backend:8080;` with a literal hostname is resolved when nginx loads the config. If the backend container is recreated (new IP on the Compose network), /api/ returns 502 until nginx restarts. If `backend` is not resolvable when the frontend container starts, nginx fails with 'host not found in upstream'.
findings.suggestion: Use Docker's resolver with a variable: `resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s; set $backend http://backend:8080; proxy_pass $backend;`. Keep the request URI unchanged, which holds with no URI part. Update container-config.test.ts to match.

findings.title: index.html served without no-cache; after a deploy, clients can keep a stale shell pointing at removed hashed assets
findings.evidence: `location / { try_files $uri /index.html; }` sets no Cache-Control, so browsers may heuristically cache index.html from Last-Modified. Meanwhile `/assets/` returns `=404` for missing hashed files, which is deliberate. A cached old index.html then requests old bundle names and gets 404s, leaving a blank app.
findings.suggestion: Add `add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;` for the index.html fallback. Because an add_header inside a location drops the server-level headers, repeat them there via an include snippet, or set the header with `expires -1` / a `map` on $uri at server level.

findings.title: Provenance scope misses text-format workbook content outside the listed roots, and exempts all of docs/qa/
findings.evidence: Outside FIXTURE_ROOTS and ASSET_ROOTS, only `MEDIA` extensions are checked. Workbook text or answer keys committed as `.json/.csv/.txt/.md/.docx/.heic/.xlsx`, e.g. `src/features/task/__fixtures__/tasks.json` or `e2e/data/answers.csv`, are never in scope. `OUT_OF_SCOPE = ['docs/qa/', 'contract/']` also exempts any PDF or scan dropped under docs/qa/. CA-D21/NFR-4 is about workbook text and answer keys, not only binaries.
findings.suggestion: Add common fixture-like locations (`**/__fixtures__/**`, `**/fixtures/**`, `src/test/**` data files, `e2e/data/**`) and document/office/image extensions (docx, xlsx, odt, heic, epub, djvu, zip) to the scope. Limit the docs/qa exemption to known generated formats (e.g. `.webm`/`.png` under docs/qa/recordings).

findings.title: A licensed asset whose own filename contains 'licence'/'OFL' passes as its own licence file
findings.evidence: `if (!e.origin.startsWith('licensed:') || LICENCE_TEXT.test(<filename>)) continue;` skips the licence-beside check for any file whose name matches `/licen[cs]e|OFL|COPYING/i`. A font named `OFLSans.woff2` or an image `license-badge.png` marked `licensed:` therefore needs no licence file.
findings.suggestion: Identify licence files by text extension plus name (e.g. `/(licen[cs]e|OFL|COPYING)[^/]*\.(txt|md)$|^(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING)$/i`), not by the name alone.

findings.title: contract-client unit test depends on a gitignored file produced only by api:generate
findings.evidence: `readFileSync(GENERATED, 'utf8')` reads `src/api/generated/schema.d.ts`, which the generator header says is gitignored. `test:run` / `test:coverage` (`vitest run`) never run `api:generate`. On a fresh clone, or with the battery's unit step before typecheck, the test throws ENOENT instead of a clear assertion.
findings.suggestion: Run `api:generate` in a Vitest globalSetup or as a `pretest:run` script, or `expect(existsSync(GENERATED)).toBe(true)` first with a message pointing to `npm run api:generate`.

findings.title: Czech and English catalogs merged into one flat object; a duplicate key silently overrides
findings.evidence: `export const messages = { ...cs, ...en };` lets a key defined in both (e.g. a shared `app.*` key added to en) silently replace the Czech value in the child UI. TypeScript does not flag it. Nothing stops child screens from rendering admin (English) keys either, and the namespacing convention exists only in comments.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test asserting the key sets of cs and en are disjoint, and that en keys start with `admin.` and cs keys with `app.`/`child.`. Alternatively type the catalogs with template-literal key types.

findings.title: The NFR-3/NFR-4 provenance scan skips docs/qa/, where the committed recordings and screenshots are written, and the recorder doesn't run the real-name guard
findings.evidence: OUT_OF_SCOPE = ['docs/qa/', 'contract/'] removes every file under docs/qa/ from the media scan. scripts/record-demos.mjs:16-29,76,89 writes docs/qa/<outDir>/<id>.webm and <id>.png there, and .gitignore only ignores the **/raw/ intermediate. The recorder opens its own browser context, so e2e/fixtures/test.ts's expectNoRealName never runs on it (grep finds no expectNoRealName or DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME in scripts/). Scenario: a developer records demos against the real home stack (seeded with the child's real display name, or with a real workbook page uploaded through FR-1) and commits the clips. No check flags the child's name or the copyrighted page in the committed PNG or WebM.
findings.suggestion: Keep docs/qa/ media in the provenance scope: list recordings in a generated manifest checked against an allowed recordings dir, or require recordings to come from the seeded fictional stack. Make record-demos.mjs run the same real-name guard on every clip before it saves the still or video, and fail when DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME is unset against a live stack.

findings.title: nginx forwards client-supplied X-Forwarded-For, so per-IP login throttling can be spoofed
findings.evidence: proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for appends the peer address to whatever X-Forwarded-For header the client sends. src/test/container-config.test.ts:37 locks this choice in. If the backend's admin-login brute-force protection or audit logging reads the client IP from X-Forwarded-For (Spring forward-headers-strategy / RemoteIpValve takes the leftmost untrusted value), any device on the LAN can send a new fake X-Forwarded-For on every attempt and avoid per-IP lockout on /api/admin login. I couldn't open the backend repo to confirm how it reads the client IP.
findings.suggestion: Overwrite the header at the edge: proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr (and X-Real-IP $remote_addr). Update container-config.test.ts to require that. Make sure the backend trusts only the nginx container as the proxy.

findings.title: Literal UI text outside .tsx JSX gets past both the NFR-9 lint rule and the pseudo-catalog test
findings.evidence: The rule only covers files: ['src/**/*.tsx'], and literalTexts() (eslint-rules/no-literal-ui-text.js:41-58) only resolves Literal, Template, Conditional, Logical and Binary nodes. Three cases it misses: `const LABEL = 'Uložit'` in a .ts module or a top-level const, rendered as {LABEL}; `document.title = 'Doučko – admin'` in a .ts hook; and a CallExpression such as {fmt('bodů')} or {['Ano'].join()}. The pseudo-catalog test (src/app/i18n-coverage.test.tsx:65-71) renders each route once in its initial state with no backend data, so a literal in a loading, error, empty or post-interaction branch never renders and the test passes.
findings.suggestion: Apply the rule to src/**/*.ts too, flag string literals assigned to document.title, and report Identifier children whose binding is a module-level string const. Extend the pseudo-catalog test with each route's non-default states (mocked error, empty and loaded query states) as slices add them.

findings.title: Dependency audit and backend exposure not verified in this run (tool access denied)
findings.evidence: I was not allowed to run `npm audit`, and reading ../backend (compose.yaml port binding, CORS, Spring Security config) was denied. So I can't confirm NFR-2 (that the frontend container's port 80 is published only on localhost or the LAN) or critical/high advisories in react-query, openapi-fetch or vite. Checked and clean in this diff: no VITE_* or import.meta.env use in src (no secrets in the bundle). .env and .env.* are gitignored and dockerignored, and the build stage isn't shipped. Base images are pinned by digest, and npm ci runs with --ignore-scripts. The build fails fast without contract/api/openapi.yaml. The CSP has no unsafe-inline script and sets frame-ancestors 'none'. No location-level add_header drops the security headers. /assets/ returns 404 instead of the SPA page. tsconfig.app.json keeps Node types out of app code, and test files are typed separately. The slice has no endpoints, upload handlers or dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so authz, IDOR, injection and mass assignment don't apply. No child PII in the fixtures (only the fictional name 'Agent Nova'), and no workbook content is committed.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit --omit=dev` and the backend compose review (ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0) before G-gate sign-off, and record the output under docs/qa/.

findings.title: Coverage summary
findings.evidence: There are 16 scenarios in the delta: 9 implemented (Dark OS, Light OS, Literal text is a lint error, Reduced motion, Smoke in three browsers, Licensed asset without its licence, Real name on a page, Guard not configured, Every contract path), 7 partial (No toggle, Pseudo-catalog render, axe on every route, Unlisted asset fails, Image build without the contract, API through the frontend origin, Missing asset), 0 missing and 0 contradicted. The store scenarios are covered as follows. The gamification 'Light and dark theme' scenarios target HQ, which does not exist yet; the shell-level e2e covers them. The content-authoring CA-D21 fixture scenarios are covered by src/test/provenance.test.ts. FR-58, NFR-3, NFR-4, NFR-6, NFR-9, NFR-12 and NFR-13 (plan row 44 and §2.1, frontend) each appear in a delta requirement.
findings.suggestion: No action needed. This entry records the coverage line the output contract asks for.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literal UI text outside JSX, through variables, and in .ts files
findings.evidence: The spec says: 'A lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text in `src/`.' In the code, `literalTexts()` only unwraps Literal, TemplateLiteral, Conditional, Logical, `+` and JSXExpressionContainer. These all pass the rule: `const l = 'Zavřít'; <button aria-label={l}/>`; `{'Ahoj' as string}`; `{['Ahoj']}`; `{String('Ahoj')}`; `{...{'aria-label':'Zavřít'}}`; `<input type={'submit'} value="Odeslat"/>` (staticAttribute only reads string-literal `type`); `<option label="Ahoj">` and `<track label>` (`label` is missing from DOM_TEXT_ATTRIBUTES); and non-JSX sinks such as `document.title = 'Doučko'` (App.tsx:17 uses exactly this sink, currently with t()). eslint.config.js:47 also scopes the rule to `src/**/*.tsx`, so `.ts` modules (hooks, query error mappers, toast helpers) are never checked. The scenario's five listed examples are all tested (lint-rule.test.ts) and pass, so the scenario holds. The requirement does not.
findings.suggestion: Unwrap TSAsExpression, TSSatisfiesExpression, TSNonNullExpression, ArrayExpression and spread attributes. Add `label` to DOM_TEXT_ATTRIBUTES. Report literals assigned to `document.title`. Extend `files` to `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` with a rule for string literals reaching known sinks. Add invalid cases to lint-rule.test.ts. Alternatively, narrow the requirement text to 'literal text in JSX' and make the pseudo-catalog test the backstop for everything else.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test checks only the first synchronous render and a narrow attribute set, so text can bypass the catalog
findings.evidence: The scenario requires: 'every visible text node, text attribute and the document title consists only of whole ⟦…⟧ segments'. The test calls `render(<App messages={pseudo} />)` once and reads the DOM right away. Text that appears after a query resolves, in loading or error states, or after interaction is never seen. TEXT_ATTRIBUTES leaves out `label` (option, optgroup, track) and the `value` of text inputs. COVERED allows any `\p{S}\p{P}\d` run, so a symbol-only accessible name such as `aria-label="★"` passes, and the lint rule also skips it because hasLetter is false. The not-found case (line 74) has no `texts.length > 1` guard, so an empty not-found screen passes. main.tsx wrappers are not rendered, so a literal error boundary or fallback added there would bypass the test.
findings.suggestion: Wait for async UI to settle (`await findBy…` or flush queries) and loop over the route's documented states. Add `label` and text-input `value` to TEXT_ATTRIBUTES. Assert that the not-found screen produces non-title text. Render any wrapper that main.tsx adds.

findings.title: Theme and axe e2e never cover the not-found screen
findings.evidence: The spec requires 'Every route SHALL have no serious or critical axe-core … violation in either colour scheme' and the theme scenarios require 'WHEN any route is opened'. Both specs iterate only `ROUTE_PATHS` (`['/']`). The app also serves a not-found screen for every other path (App.tsx:20, `<NotFound />`). That screen has no `data-route` marker, and neither e2e opens an unregistered path, even though the pseudo-catalog scenario explicitly includes 'an unregistered path'. axe and theme checks never run on the screen a child reaches from any bad link.
findings.suggestion: Give NotFound a marker (e.g. `data-route="*"`). Add an unregistered path such as `/no-such-route` to the iteration in a11y.spec.ts and theme.spec.ts, or to a shared e2e path list that routes.test.ts keeps in sync.

findings.title: The 'No toggle' e2e passes on zero controls and swallows click failures
findings.evidence: The scenario says: 'WHEN every button, switch, checkbox, radio, select or menu toggle on a route is activated THEN <html> never gets data-theme'. The only route (`/`, Shell.tsx) renders just an `<h1>`, so `controls.count()` is 0 and the loop body never runs. The test then passes without activating anything. Inside the loop, `control.click(...).catch(() => undefined)` also hides any control that could not be activated. Per the AGENTS.md lesson, a PASS over zero evidence is NOT-EARNED, yet the QA report lists the test as `ok` (automated-verification-latest.md:301,303).
findings.suggestion: Assert or log the number of controls exercised, and report SKIP-pending or NOT-EARNED when it is 0 instead of passing. Drop the silent `.catch` or count failures and fail on them.

findings.title: Provenance check exempts docs/qa/ and contract/, but the spec says 'anywhere else'
findings.evidence: The spec says: 'every image, font, audio, video or PDF file anywhere in the repository, SHALL be listed' and the scenario says 'or a media or PDF file anywhere else, that the manifest does not list … fails and names the file'. In the code, `const OUT_OF_SCOPE = ['docs/qa/', 'contract/'];` excludes these from `inScope`, and the test asserts `docs/qa/demo.png` is not reported (line 82). A workbook scan or PDF placed under docs/qa/ would pass. The carve-out is written in fixtures/PROVENANCE.md but not in the spec, so the two have diverged.
findings.suggestion: Either amend the spec delta to name the docs/qa/ (generated evidence) and contract/ (pinned submodule) exemptions, or narrow the exemption to the generated recording or screenshot file types and paths the recorder actually writes.

findings.title: Media extension list leaves out common workbook, image and audio/video formats
findings.evidence: The spec covers 'every image, font, audio, video or PDF file anywhere'. The MEDIA regex is `png|jpe?g|gif|webp|avif|svg|ico|bmp|tiff?|woff2?|ttf|otf|eot|pdf|mp3|wav|ogg|m4a|mp4|webm|mov`. It misses heic/heif, jxl, psd, djvu (a common scanned-workbook format, NFR-4), flac, aac, opus, avi, mkv and m4v, so such files outside the fixture and asset roots go unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Extend MEDIA, or detect binary or media files by content (e.g. the `file`/magic-bytes approach CA-D1 uses), and add those cases to the unlisted-file test.

findings.title: Licence-file heuristic skips assets whose own filename contains 'OFL' or 'license'
findings.evidence: The scenario says: 'GIVEN a licensed: asset with no licence file … listed beside it … THEN it fails'. The code skips the check with `if (!e.origin.startsWith('licensed:') || LICENCE_TEXT.test(<filename>)) continue;` where `LICENCE_TEXT = /licen[cs]e|OFL|COPYING/i`. An asset named e.g. `Foo-OFL-Regular.woff2` or `licensed-badge.svg` is treated as a licence file and never needs a real one beside it.
findings.suggestion: Treat a row as a licence file only if it has a text extension (`.txt`, `.md`, none) or the 'What' column says so. Add a test with a font named `X-OFL.woff2`.

findings.title: Proxy, missing-asset and image-build scenarios are only checked statically; the live smoke (task 4.4) is open
findings.evidence: The scenarios read: 'WHEN /api/child/nope is requested from the frontend port THEN the answer is the backend's 404 problem+json, with the security headers'; 'WHEN /assets/missing.js is requested THEN the answer is 404'; and 'GIVEN a build context without contract/api/openapi.yaml WHEN the frontend image is built THEN the build fails'. container-config.test.ts only regex-matches nginx.conf and the Dockerfile. No test sends a request through nginx or builds the image without the contract. tasks.md 4.4 ('/api/child/nope through nginx is 404 problem+json') is unticked. The behaviours the static checks cannot see (header inheritance with `expires`, duplicate headers from the backend, the try_files result) stay unverified.
findings.suggestion: Add a compose-stack e2e (run when E2E_BASE_URL is set) that requests `/api/child/nope`, `/assets/missing.js` and `/deep/link`, and asserts status, content type and the three security headers. Add a CI job that runs `docker build` with an empty `contract/` and expects failure. Tick 4.4 only once that evidence exists.

findings.title: nginx hides only the backend's X-Content-Type-Options, so other backend security headers can be duplicated or conflict
findings.evidence: The spec requires 'Every response SHALL carry … Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and a Content-Security-Policy …'. The config has only `proxy_hide_header X-Content-Type-Options;`. If the backend (Spring Security) sends Referrer-Policy, Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options on /api responses, the browser gets two copies with possibly different values. For CSP, both policies apply. The server-level comment claims the headers are deduplicated, but only one of the three is.
findings.suggestion: Also add `proxy_hide_header Referrer-Policy;` and `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy;`, or test the proxied response headers in the live smoke.

findings.title: tsconfig guard test does not check the leak it should: Node types in app code
findings.evidence: The test 'keeps DOM types out of Node-side code' only asserts that tsconfig.node.json has no DOM lib and that e2e is referenced. Nothing asserts that tsconfig.app.json `types` stays `["vite/client"]` without `node`, or that its `exclude` keeps test files out. tsconfig.test.json:6 adds `"node"` over all of `src`, so the app project is the only thing stopping `process`/`node:fs` from reaching app code, and no test guards it. The current configs are correct (tsconfig.app.json types: ["vite/client"]).
findings.suggestion: Add assertions: `json('tsconfig.app.json').compilerOptions.types` does not contain 'node', and its `exclude` covers `src/**/*.test.ts(x)` and `src/test`. Optionally add a probe file that imports `node:fs` under the app project and expect tsc to fail.

findings.title: Contract-client test checks substrings in schema.d.ts, not keys of the generated `paths` type
findings.evidence: The scenario says: 'THEN every path of the pinned contract is a key of the generated `paths` type'. The code is `schema.includes(`"${p}"`)`, which passes if the path string appears anywhere in the file (a JSDoc comment, an operationId description). The path regex `^ {2}(\/api\/[^:\s]+):` also skips any contract path not under `/api/` or indented differently, and quoted keys.
findings.suggestion: Parse the YAML (the generator already has a parser) to get `Object.keys(doc.paths)`. Check them against the generated type, e.g. with a type-level test (`expectTypeOf<keyof paths>()`) or by matching `^\s+"<path>": \{` inside the `export interface paths` block.

findings.title: Undocumented behaviour in nginx.conf: 51 MB upload cap, X-Forwarded-Proto, 1-year asset caching, extra CSP directives
findings.evidence: The 'Served behind one origin' requirement covers proxying, the SPA fallback, three headers and pinned digests. The config also sets `client_max_body_size 51m;` (NFR-17, not part of this slice), `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto`, `expires 1y` on /assets/, and CSP `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src data: blob:`, `form-action 'self'`. The upload cap and `unsafe-inline` styles are product-relevant choices with no backing requirement.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec delta (or design.md, with a requirement reference) to record the upload size limit tied to NFR-17 and the CSP style-src exception, so later slices don't diverge silently.

result.reasoning:
I confirmed the mechanism in eslint-rules/no-literal-ui-text.js:41-58. `literalTexts` only looks into Literal, TemplateLiteral, ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression, BinaryExpression with `+`, and JSXExpressionContainer. Every other node type falls to `default: return []`. So all of these pass lint even though they put text on screen:
- the TS wrappers `as`, `satisfies` and `!`
- array and object literals, such as `options={[{label:'Ano'}]}`
- call expressions, such as `'Ahoj'.toUpperCase()`
